name: Sensed-presence protocol: Thomas both sides, then Burst-X (Saroka 2015)
origin: Persinger laboratory, Laurentian University; the two-phase sensed-presence protocol as stated by Saroka (2015)
summary: The Persinger lab's two-phase sensed-presence protocol as Saroka (2015) states it: 30 min of the frequency-modulated 'Thomas' pattern across both temporoparietal regions, then 30 min of the burst-firing (Burst-X) pattern. Saroka & Persinger (2013) reported that people who sensed a presence showed a rise in coherence between the two temporal lobes about 10-15 min after the initial frequency-modulated application, with more right-frontal theta.
notes: Saroka's thesis (p. 29) gives the protocol in one sentence: 30 min of a frequency-modulated pattern ('also called the Thomas pattern') applied bilaterally over the temporo-parietal region, then 30 min of BurstX. It names no sites, intensity or intervals, so these follow the lab's other papers. Phase 1 plays the exact Thomas table (US 6,234,953 Table 1: 849 points at 3 ms, 2.55 s per cycle; Buckner 2015) with a 3-ms pause between repeats (Murugan 2013; Carniello 2020). The Burst-X point values were never published; the built-in accelerating burst stands in, with the published timing of 230 points at 3 ms (0.69 s; Carniello 2020) once every 4 s (Martin 2004); Murugan (248 points, every 3 s) and Collins 2014 (289 points) give other versions. Saroka does not say where phase 2 was applied; it stays on the same coils, both sides together (an assumption). Two static coils per side, T7/TP7 and T8/TP8, stand in for 'temporo-parietal' (like the lab's four-solenoid 'Koren boxes', Tsang 2004; the lab never published coil positions); 1 uT is the lab's usual human intensity (1-5 uT inside its solenoids, Lehman 2016). How it differs: persinger-synthetic-ghost-2000 and persinger-granqvist-2005-replication play the Thomas phase on the right only, as the lab's 2000 haunt case did, and god-helmet-classic is Murphy's Shiva version (a right-side chirp, then a burst stepping around four coils per side). The coherence and theta markers (Saroka & Persinger 2013, as Saroka summarizes them) come from one lab and were never replicated; independent double-blind tests found no field effect (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012). The 2000 case reported 'rushes of fear' during the frequency-modulated pattern, and Murphy expects his first phase to be unpleasant for some people: press Skip to go to phase 2, and stop at once on fear or distress. Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history, implanted devices, pregnancy, or anxiety or trauma symptoms; have someone nearby.
setting: Seated in a dark, quiet room with the eyes closed or covered by opaque goggles (the lab used an acoustic chamber that was also a Faraday cage, and sometimes recorded 19-channel EEG). The lab told people they might or might not receive a field; the app's Blind option does the same.
schedule: One 60-min session. For a self-test, compare it with a blinded sham session on another day and write down what you experienced before unblinding; at most weekly.
